summary: Tested new case-evaluation flow (manual evaluation + user evaluation count). Added 9 new pytest cases covering POST /api/evaluations/manual and GET /api/evaluations/user/{user_id}/count — all 9 pass. Full suite: 25/26 pass (1 pre-existing flaky LLM streaming test, unrelated). Frontend code wiring for the new flow verified by source inspection and unauthenticated route check (auth-gated by real Google OAuth so the form UI itself cannot be exercised by Playwright).

minor.issue: Pre-existing: SSE stream occasionally does not signal done within 60s on slow LLM responses. Flaky, not related to current feature.

action_items: Main agent should self-test end-to-end via real Google login: (1) start sim, (2) click Finalizar Simulación, (3) confirm redirect to /case-evaluation/:sim_id, (4) fill 5 competencies × 1 nivel, (5) submit and verify evaluation persists, (6) open Global Evaluations and verify button enables only after >=1 CASO evaluation exists.

Confirm only teachers/admins see the rubric form (CaseEvaluation page should restrict or hide for students — current backend already returns 403 for non-teacher POSTs, but frontend should also hide or warn).
Optional: harden streaming chat endpoint test timing (independent of this feature).
critical_code_review_comments: POST /api/evaluations/manual trusts user_id and case_id from the request body — should default these from the sim_doc to prevent a teacher from accidentally (or maliciously) writing an evaluation against a different user/case than the simulation actually belongs to.

Manual evaluation does not validate that scores contain exactly the 5 expected competency keys nor that values fall within the cuartil set [12.5, 37.5, 62.5, 87.5]. Add Pydantic validation/enums to mirror the frontend rubric.
evaluated_by field is a free-text string client-supplies — should derive from authenticated user.name / user.user_id for auditability.
server.py still >1400 lines — split into routers (evaluations, simulations, dashboard) for maintainability.
Frontend CaseEvaluation page is not gated by role on the client — students who somehow reach the URL would see the rubric (they would still get 403 on submit, but UX-wise it should redirect).
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_amed_api.py (appended 9 tests for manual evaluation + evaluation count)

success_rate.backend: 100% on new endpoints (9/9); 96% overall (25/26, 1 unrelated flaky)
